newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TENNIS-PIERCE OUSTS SPIRLEA IN GRAND SLAM WARM-UP.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-PIERCE OUSTS SPIRLEA IN GRAND SLAM WARM-UP.

text.p: Former Australian Open champion Mary Pierce ousted fifth seed Irina Spirlea of Romania on Sunday in a first-round upset at a warm-up event for the first Grand Slam of the season.
Pierce defeated Spirlea 6-3 4-6 6-4 on the first day of the Sydney International, a tour event for men and women before next week's Open in Melbourne.

Pierce, a 21-year-old French-American, is gradually refinding her form after a lingering shoulder injury and was match-rusty after a three-month layoff. But she still showed some of the power that won her the Open in 1995 as she built up an early 6-3 4-2 lead over Spirlea, who is ranked 10th in the world to her 24th.

But baseliner Spirlea used a fast first serve and unsettling sliced backhand to take the next four games and looked likely to repeat the three-set win she enjoyed over Pierce in the final of a tour event in Florida in April.

The third set began with four successive breaks of service before the two women brought their nerves under control and settled down to a hard-fought decider. Pierce fumbled an easy slam on her first match point but made no mistake with her second and broke Spirlea's serve to take the final set 6-4.

Pierce said she was still suffering from the shoulder weakness which has kept her out of competitive tennis for the past three months and hoped to use the Sydney tournament to play "a lot of tough matches against a lot of tough girls".

Pierce's second round opponent will be Yayuk Basuki of Indonesia, who defeated Australia's Nicole Bradtke 6-3 3-6 6-0. Bradtke, 27, has also had persistent shoulder problems and said she would decide after January 13-26 Australian Open whether to continue in the game.
"I don't know what I'm doing or where I'm going," said a dejected Bradtke.
Top women seeds Arantxa Sanchez Vicario, Martina Hingis, Iva Majoli and Lindsay Davenport have all received byes into the second round and are not expected to play before Tuesday.

The men's top seed is Croatia's Goran Ivanisevic ahead of South Africa's Wayne Ferreira and Spain's Alberto Costa. Ivanisevic was expected to start his campaign against Marc-Kevin Goellner of Germany on Monday. REUTER
